scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The map label Anggamudi is linked to Angkamuthi through the AIATSIS spelling guide and contemporary community self-identification. The guide is not used to collapse Atampaya, Nggamadi or every neighboring group into one entity.

Imported snapshots cover 1600 to 1815 in northern Cape York. No sourced event dates the people’s beginning to 1600 or their disappearance to 1815. Later documented periods are deliberately not back-projected into those years.

Seven Rivers supplies a public community account. Restricted cultural places are not described beyond public generalities, and no precise locations, access claims or ritual details are invented. Its territorial description does not certify the imported polygon.

Cowal Creek/Injinoo was and is shared by several peoples. The 1915 reserve is an administrative event, not the origin of Angkamuthi society. The Queensland historical account is used for dated settlement and trade evidence, not its quoted colonial extinction claims.

Only the public MS 1002 finding aid was read. Story titles establish subjects, not detailed content. Crowley’s finding aid explicitly warns that uncorrected field notes contain inconsistencies; no uncertain linguistic form or translation is reproduced. The card uses under 100 derived words from this source to allow a separate Anguthimri card.

The college’s 2015 language-renewal account names Sandra Sebasio and neighboring Elders. Current publication does not establish that every named participant is alive today. Injinoo Ikya, named clan languages and Creoles are not equated indiscriminately.

Ropeyarn’s own printed transcript was read; the audio was not played. AGSA and QAGOMA give different work dimensions, so no size is supplied. Published motifs and process are described without extending to restricted cultural knowledge.

The ranger report is a dated first-person operational account by Angelina Williams. It distinguishes ongoing work, proposals and challenges. Claims do not imply every ranger has the same ancestry or that every listed action was completed everywhere.

TropWATER’s indexed project text was read when direct opening failed. The December 2024 findings concern defined survey sites. Planned training and bilingual outputs are distinguished from completed surveys, and the August 2026 update precedes this research date.
The grocery account is a service provider’s report of a specific project, not an independent evaluation of prices, food security or present inventory.
The 2025 authorization notice does not establish a meeting result, application filing or native title determination. No successor links or legal boundary changes are inferred.
Independent historical review, border assessment and depth certification remain pending.
